question: A T-square is used mainly to draw:
answer: Horizontal lines
explanation: The T-square slides along the board edge and its blade draws horizontal lines.

question: Which pair of set squares is standard?
explanation: These two give 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees, and combinations of them give other angles.

question: When using a compass the needle point should be:
options: Level with the pencil lead and sharp
answer: Level with the pencil lead and sharp
explanation: If the needle and lead are not level the centre shifts and the circle is inaccurate.

question: A French curve is used to draw:
answer: Smooth irregular curves
explanation: French curves give smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass.

question: Which pencil grade is used for construction lines?
answer: Harder and lighter
explanation: Harder leads give light lines that are easily erased, and construction lines must not show in the finished drawing.

question: A divider is used to:
answer: Transfer distances
explanation: Dividers step off and transfer distances accurately.

question: A hidden edge is shown by:
answer: A thin short-dashed line
explanation: Dashed lines show edges that cannot be seen from the viewing direction.

question: A chain line with long and short dashes is used for:
answer: Centre lines and cutting planes
explanation: Chain lines mark axes of symmetry and the paths of cutting planes.

question: The title block of a drawing normally carries:
options: Title, scale, date, drawing number and name
answer: Title, scale, date, drawing number and name
explanation: The title block identifies the drawing and records who drew it and when.

question: Dimension figures on a drawing state:
options: The measured length on the sheet
The true size of the feature
answer: The true size of the feature
explanation: Dimensions always give the real dimension, whatever the scale.

question: Standard technical lettering is:
options: Single-stroke Gothic capitals, upright or inclined
answer: Single-stroke Gothic capitals, upright or inclined
explanation: Single-stroke letters are quick to draw and easy to read.

question: Adjacent letters and words in standard lettering should be:
options: Spaced so the text is legible
All the same height as the drawing
answer: Spaced so the text is legible
explanation: Letter and word spacing is part of legibility.

question: A drawing at a scale of 1:50 means:
options: The drawing is fifty times the object
Every drawn length is one fiftieth of the real length
The object is fifty metres long
answer: Every drawn length is one fiftieth of the real length
explanation: The first figure refers to the drawing and the second to the object.

question: A wall 4 m long drawn at 1:20 measures:
answer: 200 mm
explanation: 4000 mm divided by 20 gives 200 mm on the sheet.

question: Which scale suits a small machined component needing detail?
explanation: An enlargement scale shows small parts clearly.

question: If a drawing is marked NTS it means:
answer: Not to scale
explanation: Such dimensions must never be scaled from the drawing.

question: The overall length of a room 6 m x 4 m drawn at 1:50 gives a drawn area of:
answer: 96 square centimetres
explanation: Drawn dimensions are 120 mm by 80 mm, giving 9600 mm2 = 96 cm2.

question: The angle between the sides of a regular hexagon is:
answer: 120 degrees
explanation: For a regular hexagon the interior angle is 120 degrees.

question: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is found by:
options: 360 divided by the number of sides
180 divided by the number of sides
90 divided by the number of sides
answer: 360 divided by the number of sides
explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon total 360 degrees.

question: A triangle can be constructed from all of these EXCEPT:
options: Two sides and the included angle
answer: Three angles only
explanation: Three angles fix the shape but not the size, so an infinite number of similar triangles results.

question: To bisect an angle you use:
options: A compass and a straight edge only
answer: A compass and a straight edge only
explanation: Arcs struck from the vertex and from points on the arms locate the bisector.

question: A perpendicular bisector of a line is the locus of points:
options: At a fixed distance from one end
Equidistant from both ends of the line
answer: Equidistant from both ends of the line
explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from each end.

question: A tangent to a circle:
options: Cuts the circle at two points
Touches the circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius there
answer: Touches the circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius there
explanation: The tangent-radius relationship is the basis of all tangent constructions.

question: A straight line joining two points on the circumference is a:
answer: Chord
explanation: A chord spans the circle without passing through the centre.

question: The centre of a blending arc joining two straight lines lies:
options: At the intersection of lines drawn parallel to the given lines at the arc radius
answer: At the intersection of lines drawn parallel to the given lines at the arc radius
explanation: Offsetting both lines by the arc radius locates the blending centre.

question: A smooth join between a straight line and an arc must be:
options: Tangential, with the tangency point marked
answer: Tangential, with the tangency point marked
explanation: Only a tangential join gives a smooth transition without a visible kink.

question: A quadrant of a circle is:
answer: A quarter of the circumference
explanation: Four quadrants make the full circle.

question: A locus is:
options: The path traced by a point moving according to a rule
answer: The path traced by a point moving according to a rule
explanation: Loci describe the motion of points in mechanisms.

question: The path traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line is a:
answer: Cycloid
explanation: The cycloid is the basis of many gear tooth profiles.

question: A cut through a cone parallel to one side produces a:
answer: Parabola
explanation: The parabola results when the cutting plane is parallel to the sloping side.

question: A cut through a cone at an angle steeper than the side and cutting both parts of a double cone produces a:
answer: Hyperbola
explanation: This cut intersects both nappes, giving the two branches of a hyperbola.

question: An ellipse can be constructed by the:
answer: Concentric circle method
explanation: The concentric circle and trammel methods both give an accurate ellipse.

question: The path of a point on a ladder sliding down a wall is part of:
answer: An ellipse
explanation: The point traces a quarter ellipse.

question: In third angle projection the plan is placed:
answer: Above the front view
explanation: In third angle the view is placed on the same side as the direction of sight.

question: In first angle projection the view from the left of an object is placed:
options: On the left of the front view
On the right of the front view
answer: On the right of the front view
explanation: First angle projection reverses the placement, so the left view appears on the right.

question: The projection symbol on a drawing shows a truncated cone and identifies:
options: Whether first or third angle is used
answer: Whether first or third angle is used
explanation: The way the small end of the cone faces shows the system used.

question: The height of a feature is transferred to a side view from the:
answer: Front view
explanation: Heights come from the front view; depths come from the plan.

question: Hidden lines in orthographic views are:
options: Drawn as thin dashed lines where edges are concealed
answer: Drawn as thin dashed lines where edges are concealed
explanation: They show internal or concealed edges that the view cannot see.

question: The correct drawing order for an orthographic drawing is:
options: Outline, then construction lines, then dimension
Construction and projection lines lightly, outline last, then dimension
answer: Construction and projection lines lightly, outline last, then dimension
explanation: Working from light construction lines to a firm outline prevents mistakes.

question: An auxiliary view is used to show:
options: A larger scale of the whole object
The true shape of an inclined face
answer: The true shape of an inclined face
explanation: The auxiliary plane is set parallel to the inclined face so it is not foreshortened.

question: Foreshortening means a feature appears:
options: Shorter or distorted because the viewing plane is not parallel to it
answer: Shorter or distorted because the viewing plane is not parallel to it
explanation: Inclined faces do not show true shape in the principal views.

question: A missing view is reconstructed by:
options: Projecting heights and depths from the given views
answer: Projecting heights and depths from the given views
explanation: Each feature point is projected across from the views that show it.

question: The first auxiliary view is taken from:
options: The principal view in which the inclined face appears as a line
answer: The principal view in which the inclined face appears as a line
explanation: The edge view of the face is the correct starting point.

question: True length of an inclined line can be found by projecting from the view in which the line appears:
options: As a point or with its other projection available for measurement
answer: As a point or with its other projection available for measurement
explanation: True length construction measures from a reference line to each end of the line.

question: Material cut by a cutting plane in a section is shown by:
answer: Hatching with thin continuous lines
explanation: Hatching is evenly spaced at 45 degrees.

question: In a section of an assembly, adjacent parts are hatched:
answer: In opposite directions
explanation: Alternating hatch direction distinguishes mating parts.

question: Which part is normally NOT hatched in a section?
options: A shaft or bolt cut longitudinally
answer: A shaft or bolt cut longitudinally
explanation: Shafts, bolts, rivets and webs are left unhatched by convention.

question: A half section is useful because it:
options: Shows external shape on one half and internal detail on the other
answer: Shows external shape on one half and internal detail on the other
explanation: It gives both external and internal information in one view.

question: Dimensions should be taken from:
options: One feature to the next in a chain where possible
answer: A datum or common reference
explanation: Datum dimensioning avoids accumulation of errors and reflects function.

question: A dimension must appear:
answer: Once only, and be complete
explanation: Duplicated or missing dimensions both cause errors in manufacture.

question: In isometric drawing the three axes are at:
answer: 120 degrees to each other
explanation: One axis is vertical and the other two are at 30 degrees above the horizontal.

question: In isometric projection the axes are drawn at:
options: True length reduced by about 82 per cent
answer: True length reduced by about 82 per cent
explanation: Isometric projection uses the adjustment; isometric drawing uses true length along the axes.

question: A circle on an isometric face is drawn as:
answer: An ellipse
explanation: The circle appears foreshortened as an ellipse on each isometric plane.

question: A non-isometric line in an isometric drawing:
options: Does not appear at true length and must be plotted from co-ordinates
answer: Does not appear at true length and must be plotted from co-ordinates
explanation: Lines not parallel to an isometric axis are distorted.

question: Hidden detail in a pictorial drawing is usually:
options: Omitted so that the view stays clear
answer: Omitted so that the view stays clear
explanation: The purpose is clarity of form.

question: Isometric drawing is commonly used for:
answer: Assembly instructions and pipe layouts
explanation: A single pictorial view communicates an arrangement quickly.

question: In cavalier oblique projection the receding lines are drawn:
answer: At full true length
explanation: Cavalier uses full depth, which is easy to measure but looks deep.

question: Cabinet oblique projection reduces the depth by:
answer: One half
explanation: Halving the depth makes the view look more natural.

question: In perspective drawing, parallel lines going away from the viewer appear to:
answer: Converge to a vanishing point
explanation: Convergence to a vanishing point is the basis of perspective.

question: A two-point perspective drawing is used for:
options: A corner view of a building
answer: A corner view of a building
explanation: Two vanishing points handle the two receding directions of a corner view.

question: The horizon line in a perspective drawing represents:
options: The eye level of the viewer
answer: The eye level of the viewer
explanation: Vanishing points lie on the horizon line at eye level.

question: Freehand sketching is useful because it:
options: Records an idea quickly and communicates it
answer: Records an idea quickly and communicates it
explanation: Sketches are used in design discussion, site notes and illustration.

question: In CAD an object snap is used to:
options: Lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
answer: Lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
explanation: Object snaps give precision without measuring.

question: Layers in a CAD drawing are used to:
options: Separate groups of entities with their own colour, line type and weight
answer: Separate groups of entities with their own colour, line type and weight
explanation: Layers let a reader show or hide what is needed and control line weights.

question: The 'offset' command is used to:
options: Draw a parallel copy at a set distance
answer: Draw a parallel copy at a set distance
explanation: Offset is used for wall thicknesses, pipes and repeated parallel lines.

question: Model space in CAD is used to:
options: Draw the geometry at full scale
answer: Draw the geometry at full scale
explanation: The layout or paper space handles the sheet and printing scale.

question: Line weights are set so that:
options: Outlines are heavy and dimension or projection lines are thin
answer: Outlines are heavy and dimension or projection lines are thin
explanation: Contrasting line weights make a drawing readable.

question: A site plan would NOT normally show:
answer: Roof truss details
explanation: Truss details belong on a roof plan and detail drawings.

question: A setback is:
options: The distance a building must be from the boundary
answer: The distance a building must be from the boundary
explanation: Planning regulations fix minimum setbacks.

question: A strip foundation is used to:
options: Spread the load of a load-bearing wall over a wider area
answer: Spread the load of a load-bearing wall over a wider area
explanation: The strip is wider than the wall so the pressure on the soil is reduced.

question: Hardcore is placed under a ground floor slab to:
answer: Provide a firm, drained base
explanation: Compacted hardcore spreads the load and allows drainage.

question: The ground floor plan is normally drawn at a scale of:
explanation: 1:50 shows room layouts and openings clearly on an A1 sheet.

question: Wall thickness, room sizes and opening widths are all dimensions found on the:
answer: Floor plan
explanation: The floor plan sets out the building.

question: A lintel is used to:
options: Support the wall below an opening
Carry the load over an opening
answer: Carry the load over an opening
explanation: The lintel spans the opening and bears on the wall at each end.

question: A damp-proof course is placed:
options: In the wall to stop moisture rising
answer: In the wall to stop moisture rising
explanation: The DPC blocks capillary movement of water up the wall.

question: Doors and windows in a building drawing set are listed in a:
answer: Schedule
explanation: The schedule gives mark, size, type and material for each opening.

question: In plan, a door symbol shows:
options: The frame, the leaf and the direction of swing
answer: The frame, the leaf and the direction of swing
explanation: Door swing must be drawn to avoid clashes with furniture and circulation.

question: Louvred windows are common in tropical buildings because they:
options: Allow ventilation while excluding rain and glare
answer: Allow ventilation while excluding rain and glare
explanation: Louvres give controlled ventilation and shading.

question: In a roof plan, a ridge line is drawn:
options: As a heavier line along the apex of two slopes
answer: As a heavier line along the apex of two slopes
explanation: Ridges, hips and valleys use conventional line weights.

question: A valley in a roof occurs where:
options: Two slopes meet at the top
Two slopes meet at the bottom of an internal corner
answer: Two slopes meet at the bottom of an internal corner
explanation: Valleys collect water and must be detailed and flashed carefully.

question: Purlins in a roof:
options: Carry the roof covering between rafters or trusses
answer: Carry the roof covering between rafters or trusses
explanation: Purlins run at right angles to rafters or trusses and support the sheeting.

question: A section drawing is used to show:
options: Heights, levels and construction cut through
answer: Heights, levels and construction cut through
explanation: A section reveals floor-to-ceiling heights, roof pitch and build-ups.

question: An elevation shows:
options: A horizontal cut through the building
The external face of the building as seen from outside
answer: The external face of the building as seen from outside
explanation: Elevations show openings, finishes, levels and roof lines on each face.

question: Levels of floors, sills and ridges are usually given relative to:
options: A datum, commonly ground floor level taken as 0
answer: A datum, commonly ground floor level taken as 0
explanation: A common datum keeps all levels consistent across the drawing set.

question: An external metric thread of 20 mm nominal diameter and 2.5 mm pitch is written:
explanation: Metric threads are designated by nominal diameter and pitch.

question: In the representation of an external thread, the major diameter is drawn:
answer: Thick continuous
explanation: The convention is the reverse for an internal thread.

question: A key and keyway are used to:
options: Transmit torque between a shaft and a hub
answer: Transmit torque between a shaft and a hub
explanation: The key prevents relative rotation.

question: Across flats is a dimension taken:
options: Across the corners of a hexagon
Between opposite flat faces of a nut or bolt head
answer: Between opposite flat faces of a nut or bolt head
explanation: Wrenches are sized by the across-flats dimension.

question: A weld symbol includes the type of weld, its size, length and:
options: Whether it is on one side or both sides
answer: Whether it is on one side or both sides
explanation: Supplementary symbols define the weld further.

question: A tolerance is:
options: The permissible variation in a dimension
answer: The permissible variation in a dimension
explanation: Every manufacturing process needs an allowed range.

question: An interference fit means:
options: There is always a gap between the parts
The shaft is always larger than the hole, so the parts must be forced or shrunk together
The parts are the same size
answer: The shaft is always larger than the hole, so the parts must be forced or shrunk together
explanation: Interference holds the parts by friction.

question: In the hole basis system:
options: The shaft size is fixed and the hole varies
The hole size is fixed and the shaft size varies
answer: The hole size is fixed and the shaft size varies
explanation: Holes are harder to machine accurately, so the hole is held constant.

question: Interchangeability of parts means:
options: Any mating part will fit without hand fitting
Parts are all the same size regardless of tolerance
answer: Any mating part will fit without hand fitting
explanation: It is what makes mass production and spares possible.

question: A bill of materials or parts list gives:
options: Item number, description, quantity and material of each part
answer: Item number, description, quantity and material of each part
explanation: It is keyed to the item numbers on the assembly drawing.

question: A revision table on a drawing records:
options: What was changed, when and by whom
answer: What was changed, when and by whom
explanation: Drawings are legal records, so changes must be traceable.

question: Three-dimensional CAD modelling is advantageous because:
options: Views, sections and pictorials are generated from the same model and stay consistent
It removes the need for dimensions
It is always faster to learn
answer: Views, sections and pictorials are generated from the same model and stay consistent
explanation: One model produces the whole coordinated drawing set.

question: Before plotting a drawing you should check:
options: Sheet size, plot scale, line weights and legibility of text
answer: Sheet size, plot scale, line weights and legibility of text
explanation: Previewing prevents a plot that cannot be read or does not fit.

question: A drawing set is normally ordered with:
options: Title sheet and drawing list, then plans, elevations, sections and details
answer: Title sheet and drawing list, then plans, elevations, sections and details
explanation: A standard order lets a reader find a drawing quickly.

question: A window schedule entry would NOT normally state:
answer: The cost of the glass
explanation: Schedules describe the opening and its component, not its price.

question: The main reason drawings are given a revision number is so that:
options: Everyone works from the same, current information
answer: Everyone works from the same, current information
explanation: Controlled revisions prevent site work from superseded drawings.
